# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# FocusArx robots.txt
# Domain: https://focusarx.site
#
# This file MUST stay consistent with the sitemap. Every URL listed in
# /sitemap.xml is allowed below, and nothing allowed here is missing from the
# sitemap. The previous version disallowed /api/ (which is where the sitemap
# was served from) while also declaring it, and blocked /dashboard while the
# sitemap listed it — contradictory signals that waste crawl budget.
#
# The sitemap is generated by the API (artifacts/api-server/src/routes/
# sitemap.ts) and rewritten to the host root by vercel.json.
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ── Default policy for all compliant crawlers ─────────────────
User-agent: *
Allow: /

# ── Redirect / utility endpoints (thin content, not for the index) ──
Disallow: /go/

# ── Private / login-walled application surfaces ───────────────
# Not indexable content: these redirect anonymous visitors to /login.
Disallow: /adminDisallow: /onboarding
Disallow: /profile
Disallow: /settings
Disallow: /notifications
Disallow: /messages
Disallow: /session-replay
Disallow: /replay
Disallow: /referral
Disallow: /wallet
Disallow: /style-guide
Disallow: /forgot-password
Disallow: /reset-password
Disallow: /auth/callback

# Login-walled product surfaces — kept out of the sitemap too.
Disallow: /dashboard
Disallow: /analytics
Disallow: /missions

Disallow: /flashcards

# ── API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Blocked wholesale except the SEO endpoints crawlers must reach.
# The sitemap is rewritten to the host root, so /api/sitemap.xml only needs
# to stay reachable as a fallback.
Disallow: /api/
Allow: /api/sitemap.xml
Allow: /api/sitemap-
Allow: /api/robots.txt
Allow: /api/og

# ── Build artifacts ───────────────────────────────────────────
Disallow: /*.map$
Disallow: /src/

# ── Advertising ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# AdSense's policy crawler must be able to load every ad-bearing page, or
# ad units stay unapproved. The old /bot/i filter 403'd AdsBot-Google at the
# server level; it is explicitly allowed here and in
# artifacts/api-server/src/middlewares/security.ts.
User-agent: AdsBot-Google
Allow: /

User-agent: Mediapartners-Google
Allow: /

# ── Search engines ────────────────────────────────────────────
User-agent: Googlebot
Allow: /
Disallow: /admin
Disallow: /api/
Allow: /api/sitemap.xml

User-agent: Bingbot
Allow: /
Disallow: /admin
Disallow: /api/
Allow: /api/sitemap.xml

# ── AI assistants / answer engines ────────────────────────────
# Deliberate ALLOW. A growing share of "how to focus" queries is answered
# inside an AI Overview or a chat assistant rather than on a results page, so
# being readable by those systems is distribution, not leakage. The pages we
# want cited are written answer-first and carry visible attribution
# (see /evidence), which is what gets a source quoted rather than skipped.
#
# Google-Extended is called out separately because it is the ONLY AI-training
# control Google offers and it does NOT affect normal Search ranking or
# AI Overviews — blocking it would cost discovery for nothing.
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin

User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin

User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin

User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin

User-agent: Claude-Web
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin

User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin

User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /
Disallow: /api/
Disallow: /admin

# ── Sitemap ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
